d: Highlighting objects lets you call attention to specific objects within your game.
h:
The Highlight instance is a visual effect which you can use to call attention to a specific object within a game. Every highlight effect has a silhouette outline that surrounds the object and a solid overlay interior that displays over the object. You can customize both of these components independently to modify the highlight's visual appearance.

Useful applications of the highlight effect include:

  • Providing visual feedback that an object is important and/or interactable.
  • Making distant objects visible through objects that are closer to the user.
  • Indicating the current position and status of other characters.

Add highlights

As a performance limit, Studio only displays 255 simultaneous Highlight instances on the client-side at a time. If you add more than this limit, the additional Highlight instances are silently ignored.

Note also that highlights on low-end devices may be more pixelated but will otherwise look the same as on other devices with any combination of settings.

Parent to objects

To add a highlight effect to an object, you can parent a new Highlight directly to the object.

  1. In the Explorer window, hover over either a Model or a BasePart, then click the ⊕ button. A contextual menu displays.
  2. From the menu, insert a Highlight. The highlight displays on the object with its default property values that create a white outline and a red tint overlay.

Set the adornee

Alternatively, you can place the Highlight instance outside of a child/parent relationship either within the workspace, StarterPlayer, StarterGui, StarterPack, or ReplicatedStorage, then set its Adornee property to the Model or BasePart that you want to highlight.

Customize highlights

You can change the properties of a Highlight instance to create interesting visual effects that properly highlight objects in theme with your game.

OutlineColor

The OutlineColor property sets the Color3 value of the highlight's outline.

OutlineTransparency

The OutlineTransparency property sets the visibility of the highlight's outline to any value between the default value of 0 (opaque) and 1 (invisible).

FillColor

The FillColor property sets the Color3 value of the highlight's interior.

FillTransparency

The FillTransparency property sets the visibility of the highlight's interior to any value between the default value of 0 (opaque) and 1 (invisible). You can use this property to determine how much of the object's existing color you want viewers to see.

DepthMode

The DepthMode property controls how the effect displays with respect to other objects in the world.

  • AlwaysOnTop — Allows the highlight to display regardless if there are objects between the camera and the highlighted object. This means the viewer is always able to see the highlight regardless of what is between the highlighted object and the camera.

  • Occluded — Hides the highlight if there are objects between the camera and the highlighted object. This means the viewer is only able to see the object if there are no obstructing objects between the highlighted object and the camera's view.

Enabled

The Enabled property allows you to quickly enable or disable the highlight without any impact on performance.

While a disabled Highlight doesn't display, it still takes one of the 255 available Highlight slots. If you plan to permanently disable a Highlight instance, it's best to delete the highlight rather than disable it.

Performance tips

While you have a lot of options to customize Highlight instances, the following tips are recommended to increase your game's performance on all devices:

  • Adding or removing a Highlight can cause a geometry rebuilding step that might lead to performance spikes and extra draw calls. If you want to change a Highlight instance's appearance or temporarily hide/display it on an object, it's best to customize the properties of the Highlight instance directly, as changing any property of the Highlight instance is lightweight and doesn't impact performance.

  • Roblox draws objects in a back to front order, which can cause problems if you embed objects with a child Highlight inside other objects that also have children Highlight instances. For this reason, it's best to keep objects with Highlight instances outside of a parent/child relationship with other objects with Highlight instances.

  • The first Highlight rendered on the screen incurs most of the performance cost (up to 1 millisecond of GPU time on mobile devices). For additional highlights beyond the first, you should not see a significant performance impact on any platform.

  • On mobile devices, highlights are more costly on performance when they cover more of the screen. On other platforms, highlights have the same performance cost regardless of their screen coverage.

  • On all platforms, highlights that are not visible on the screen (whether disabled or fully transparent) incur no performance cost.

kid.simple: A `Highlight` adds a glowing outline and a colored overlay to a part or model. It is used to show that something is important, can be picked up, or to let players see teammates through walls. You can change the outline color, the fill color, how see-through each is, and whether it shows through other objects. It is easy to add and cheap to turn on and off.
kid.analogy: It is like using a highlighter pen on a page: it draws attention to the important part so your eyes find it right away.
keyPoints: Every highlight has an outline around the object and a fill that covers the object.
Add one by putting a `Highlight` inside a model or part, or place it elsewhere and set its `Adornee` to the object.
`OutlineColor` and `FillColor` set the colors. `OutlineTransparency` and `FillTransparency` go from 0 (solid) to 1 (invisible).
`DepthMode = AlwaysOnTop` shows the highlight even through walls. `Occluded` hides it when something is in the way.
Use `Enabled` to turn it on and off. This costs almost nothing.
Only 255 highlights can show at once on a player's screen. Extra ones are silently ignored, even disabled ones still take a slot.
For better performance, change properties instead of adding and removing highlights, and avoid putting highlighted objects inside other highlighted objects.

terms.outline: The colored line drawn around the edge of the object.
terms.fill / interior: The color layer drawn over the object itself.
terms.transparency: How see-through something is. 0 is solid, 0.5 is half see-through, 1 is invisible.
terms.Adornee: The object a highlight is attached to, when the highlight is not inside that object.
terms.DepthMode: Whether the highlight can be seen through walls (AlwaysOnTop) or only when nothing blocks it (Occluded).
terms.client-side: On each player's own device. The 255 limit counts the highlights one player's screen is showing.
terms.performance spike: A sudden moment of lag. Adding or removing highlights can cause one.

example.title: Highlight a treasure chest when a player gets close
example.place: LocalScript in StarterPlayerScripts (with a model named Chest in Workspace)
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local chest = workspace:WaitForChild("Chest")

local highlight = Instance.new("Highlight")
highlight.FillColor = Color3.fromRGB(255, 215, 0) -- gold
highlight.FillTransparency = 0.6
highlight.OutlineColor = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
highlight.DepthMode = Enum.HighlightDepthMode.Occluded
highlight.Enabled = false
highlight.Parent = chest

RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
	local character = player.Character
	local root = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if root then
		local distance = (root.Position - chest:GetPivot().Position).Magnitude
		highlight.Enabled = distance < 15 -- glow when within 15 studs
	end
end)
explain: This is a LocalScript, so only this player sees the glow.
We create one `Highlight` with a gold fill and a white outline, and put it in the chest.
It starts turned off with `Enabled = false`.
Every frame we measure how far the player is from the chest.
If they are closer than 15 studs, we turn the highlight on; otherwise we turn it off. Toggling `Enabled` is cheap, so this is fine.

watchOut: Do not create and destroy highlights over and over. Make one and toggle `Enabled` instead.
A disabled highlight still uses one of the 255 slots. Delete highlights you will never use again.
If players can see something through walls by accident, check that `DepthMode` is not `AlwaysOnTop`.
